sources.news_title: Five injured, one critically, in shooting at Virginia State University
sources.text:
VIRGINIA - Five people have been injured, one critically, in a shooting at Virginia State University which involved multiple suspects, the university has said. Officers responded to the incident outside a residence halls at about 01:28 local time (05:28 GMT) on Saturday. Five individuals, who were all found with gunshot wounds, were taken to local hospitals. Four had injuries which were not deemed to be life-threatening, the university said.
It was not immediately clear if any suspects have been arrested. The BBC has approached local police for comment.
A temporary lockdown on the campus has since been lifted but a “significant” law enforcement presence is still on site, the university confirmed in a statement. It added that Chesterfield County Police are leading the investigation with help from other local law enforcement and campus police. Virginia State University (VSU) has about 5,000 students and is just over 20 miles south of Richmond, the capital of the US state of Virginia.
It is also one of the country’s historically black colleges and universities. Such institutions were created to provide higher education to disenfranchised African Americans, who were otherwise prohibited from attending most colleges.
According to the university’s website, classes for the new term were set to begin on Monday and campus dormitories opened for returning students on Friday.

sources.news_title: At least one student among five people shot at Virginia State University
sources.text:
Five people were wounded in a shooting involving multiple suspects at Virginia State University early on Saturday (August 15, 2026), prompting a campus lockdown and police investigation just as students got ready for a new school year.
It happened near the university's Quad Annexes, where campus police and Chesterfield County officers discovered five people suffering from gunshot wounds outside campus dormitories. At least one of the wounded people was later confirmed to be a student, the university said in a statement.

The shooting was still under investigation later on Saturday (August 15, 2026) and happened as Virginia State's academic year begins. According to the university's website, residence halls opened for students a week ago, and classes resume on Monday (August 17, 2026). Many students had just completed the university's “New Trojans Experience" for incoming students.
Police and university officials have not identified any of the victims. The five were taken to hospitals, and one initially listed as having life-threatening injuries has been upgraded to critical condition, county police said.
The others sustained non-life-threatening injuries, police said. The person confirmed to be a student was among those whose injuries were not life-threatening, and the student has been released from a hospital, the university said.
The university said in a statement early on Saturday (August 15, 2026) that the shooting involves "multiple suspects". It said in a statement later in the day that law enforcement did not believe there was an immediate threat to the campus community, and a campus lockdown had been lifted.
"We recognize the concern this incident has caused among our students, parents, alumni, friends, and the broader VSU community," the university statement said. "The safety and well-being of our students remain our highest priority." The campus had a large law enforcement presence on Saturday (August 15, 2026) morning, and the university informed students that they should monitor their email for additional safety measures and information about support services. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Hanover County Sheriff's Office were assisting, county police said.
Virginia State University is a historically Black university located in Ettrick, Virginia, about 24 miles south of the State capital of Richmond. The public university has about 5,700 students and was the first fully state-supported four-year college for Black Americans. Most of its students are undergraduates.
The university has grown in recent years while attempting to improve safety and retain its historic charm, said Arthur Fridrich, the university's former director of distance education, who lives near the campus and visits regularly. A shooting like this just as students return for classes is heartbreaking for the community, he said.
"To start a new year with this event is very tragic. It casts a shadow in the minds of all students, and for some it will be difficult to rid their minds of this term," Fridrich said. "For those that were shot, my heart bleeds. I hope that they all mend and somehow do not let this event define their lives." Gov Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, said via social media that she and her husband were "praying for a quick recovery for those who were shot this morning at Virginia State University, and our thoughts are with the VSU community." She also thanked first responders and law enforcement.
Sen Mark Warner, also a Democrat, said it was "devastating to see another Virginia campus harmed by gun violence."

sources.news_title: Multiple shooters STILL at large after rampage at Virginia State University days before classes begin
sources.text:
Multiple gunmen remained at large Saturday evening after five people were shot in the early morning hours at Virginia State University, just days before the start of the new academic year.
According to a report from the Daily Mail, the attack unfolded around 1:30 a.m. near campus dormitories in the university’s Quad Annexes. Campus police and Chesterfield County officers found the five victims suffering from gunshot wounds. None of the victims died, though one remained in critical condition in hospital as of Saturday evening. The others sustained non-life-threatening injuries.
At least one of those wounded was confirmed to be a student. That individual, whose injuries were not life-threatening, has since been released from the hospital, the university said. Authorities have not publicly identified any of the victims.
The shooting came as new freshmen arrived on campus. Many students had completed the university’s “New Trojans Experience” for incoming students only hours earlier, receiving university pins and hearing a speech from former NFL quarterback Cam Newton. Residence halls had opened a week earlier, with classes set to resume on Monday.
University officials stated early Saturday that the incident involved “multiple suspects.” No information about the shooters has been released, and there was no indication police had identified any suspects.
Police later determined there was no immediate threat to the campus community and lifted a lockdown. “VSU Police will maintain an increased presence on campus as the investigation continues,” the university said in a statement.
“Students should monitor their VSU email for additional safety measures currently in effect and information about available support resources. Although the lockdown has been lifted, members of the VSU community are asked to remain mindful of the ongoing law enforcement activity and avoid the immediate area where investigators are processing the scene.”
Virginia State University has a history of gun violence. Five people were wounded in three separate attacks in 2022, and one person was wounded and another killed near campus last year.
Local leaders expressed shock and offered support. “Virginia State University is my alma mater. Waking up to this news is heartbreaking,” said Rozia Henson, a Democratic member of the Virginia House of Delegates. “My prayers are with everyone affected this morning, with their families, and with the entire Trojan family. VSU, we are with you.”

A significant law-enforcement presence remained on campus as investigators processed the scene. VSU Police, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Hanover County Sheriff’s Office were assisting Chesterfield County Police.

Incoming students had just completed the university’s New Trojans Experience. Fall classes are scheduled to begin Monday.
Authorities had not publicly identified any of the five victims. The investigation remained focused on multiple suspects, with no immediate threat believed to be facing the wider campus community after the lockdown ended.
The timing makes the violence especially jarring. Thousands of students and families were arriving on campus for what should have been the beginning of a new chapter.

On the school’s Facebook page, worried parents posted prayers and frustrations, despondent that the students’ first weekend was marred by violence.
“This is sad. I was just on campus yesterday with my son,” one woman wrote.
“We just dropped our daughter off hours before this happened,” wrote another. “There needs to be heightened security for the campus. Period.”
One alumnus wrote that he and his wife had visited campus for a “stroll down ‘beautiful memories lane’”.
“When these type of events happen it’s terrifying to know that students, faculty, and visitors cannot enjoy the same level of peace that we had while we were there,” he added. “Prayers for the VSU community, immediate and extended.”
About 5700 students attend Virginia State, a historically black college and university  a 30-minute drive from Richmond.
The school has endured several incidents of gun violence on or near its campus in recent years. In 2024, it locked down at least three times because of gunfire that left five people, including a teenager, injured. In 2025, someone was shot in the leg near a campus basketball court, and a man was killed in a parking lot close to the school.
Virginia State also locked down and cancelled classes in September last year because it and several other HBCUs across the country received violent threats.

sources.text:
Manhunt underway after 5 shot outside Virginia State University dorms
Petersburg, Virginia - Multiple suspects are still at large after a mass shooting at Virginia State University that left multiple people hospitalized and one in critical condition.
In an X post shared on Saturday morning, the university – a historically Black college – said officers arrived at the 3300 block of Boisseau Street at 1:28 AM, where they "discovered five individuals suffering from gunshot wounds outside VSU residence halls."
The victims were transported to a local hospital, where four are recovering from non-life-threatening injuries, while the fifth is in critical condition.
Local police told the BBC on Saturday afternoon that they believe there were multiple suspects.
A lockdown was immediately initiated after the shooting, but it was lifted around 8:30 AM, despite no suspects being detained.
"We don't have anybody in custody," said Lieutenant James Lamb of the Chesterfield County Police Department. "We know there was more than one shooter, so I would say the suspects are still at large."
In a follow-up post, the university confirmed that at least one of the victims was a VSU student, who has recently been released from the hospital. Lamb has also said that at least one of the victims was a minor.
The school – which is scheduled to begin classes on Monday – further said: "Law enforcement does not believe there is an immediate threat to the VSU campus community."
This is a developing story.

Five Injured In Virginia State University Shooting; Multiple Gunmen Sought
by Stefan J. Bos, Worthy News Chief International Correspondent
WASHINGTON (Worthy News) – Five people were injured, one critically, in a shooting involving multiple gunmen at Virginia State University early Saturday, authorities said, a day after six people, including a suspected shooter, died in separate shootings in Michigan.
Officers responded at about 1:28 a.m. local time to reports of gunfire near the Quad Annexes, a residential area on the Virginia State University (VSU) campus, where they found five people suffering from gunshot wounds outside residence halls.
All five were taken to hospitals, with one listed in critical condition while the other four suffered injuries that were not considered life-threatening, university officials said.
Investigators said they believed more than one shooter was involved, but no arrests had been announced by Saturday afternoon.
“We don’t have anybody in custody,” Lieutenant James R. Lamb of the Chesterfield County Police Department said. “We know there was more than one shooter, so I would say the suspects are still at large.”
MULTIPLE SHOOTERS SOUGHT
Lamb said investigators were reviewing surveillance footage for evidence and were not treating any of the five wounded people as suspects.
At least one of the victims is a Virginia State University student, while another is under 18, according to police.
A temporary lockdown imposed following the shooting was lifted around 9 a.m., although authorities said a significant law enforcement presence remained on campus.
Chesterfield County Police were leading the investigation with assistance from university police and other law enforcement agencies, including federal authorities.
The shooting came as students were returning to campus ahead of the fall semester, with residence halls opening Friday and classes scheduled to begin Monday.
STUDENTS RETURNING TO CAMPUS
Virginia State University, located in Ettrick just over 20 miles (32 kilometers) south of Richmond, Virginia’s capital, has roughly 5,000 students.
It is one of America’s historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs), institutions established when racial discrimination and segregation prevented many African Americans from attending other colleges and universities.
The violence came a day after a series of shootings in rural Missaukee County in northern Michigan left five victims and the suspected gunman dead and another person critically wounded.
Michigan State Police identified the suspected shooter as 39-year-old Chad Hickman after an extensive search involving several crime scenes.
Police responding Friday to a home in Missaukee County, about 170 miles (270 kilometers) northwest of Detroit, initially found three people dead and another critically wounded.
SIX DEAD IN MICHIGAN
As authorities searched for Hickman, another victim was found dead at a separate location before police located the suspect’s vehicle near Whitlock Lake.
Police later found Hickman dead in a wooded area along with another deceased person, bringing the death toll, including the suspected gunman, to six.
Authorities were investigating the circumstances surrounding the killings and had not publicly established a motive.
The Virginia and Michigan violence followed another deadly shooting earlier this month in Prospect Hill, a rural community in North Carolina’s Caswell County.
Authorities initially described the August 5 violence as a “mass shooting,” but the county sheriff later characterized it as a domestic family incident.
NORTH CAROLINA FAMILY SHOOTING
Four adult members of the same family were shot at a home in the Prospect Hill community, authorities said.
Three people died, including the suspected shooter, while a fourth person was hospitalized with a gunshot wound.
The North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation assisted the Caswell County Sheriff’s Office with the investigation.
Authorities said at the time that the violence was contained to the home and there was no continuing threat to the wider community.
The latest shootings added to continuing concerns about gun violence in the United States as investigators sought those responsible for Saturday’s shooting at Virginia State University.
INVESTIGATION CONTINUES
Authorities urged anyone with information about the Virginia State University shooting to contact investigators as police continued reviewing evidence and surveillance footage.
No motive for the campus shooting had been announced by Saturday.

sources.news_title: VSU Shooting: One Critical, Lockdown Lifted, Suspects Sought
sources.text:
A 19-year-old man not enrolled at Virginia State University was arrested Saturday afternoon after he was found hiding in a dormitory closet, more than 12 hours after five people were shot near campus residence halls in an attack that left one victim in critical condition and prompted a campus-wide lockdown.
Chesterfield County Police identified the suspect as Camron Harris of Henrico, Virginia. Officers located him inside a closet in Seward Hall, a residence hall on the university's campus in Ettrick, at approximately 4 p.m. Saturday, roughly 15 hours after the shooting was first reported. He was taken to the Chesterfield County Jail, where authorities obtained eight felony warrants against him — four counts of malicious wounding and four counts of use of a firearm in the commission of a felony. Harris is being held without bond. It was not immediately clear Saturday evening whether he had retained an attorney able to speak on his behalf.
The shooting occurred shortly after 1:28 a.m. Saturday, when officers responding to the 3300 block of Boisseau Street, near the university's Quad Annexes, found five people with gunshot wounds outside VSU's residence halls. All five were transported to area hospitals. One victim, initially described by authorities as having life-threatening injuries, was later listed in critical condition. The other four sustained non-life-threatening injuries. According to Chesterfield County Police, Harris is not a VSU student, and neither were four of the five people he is accused of shooting; only one of the victims, a 20-year-old man, is a student at the university, and he has since been released from the hospital. The remaining victims ranged in age from 17 to 23 and included a 21-year-old man with critical injuries, a 23-year-old man and a 19-year-old woman with non-life-threatening injuries, and a 17-year-old male. The victims' names have not been released, and authorities have given no information about a possible motive for the shooting.
VSU Police Chief David Bragg lifted the campus lockdown around 8:20 a.m. Saturday, about seven hours after officers first responded to the scene, though the university continued to ask students, faculty and visitors to avoid the immediate area while investigators processed the scene. In a statement issued Saturday morning, before Harris's arrest, the university said the shooting had involved multiple suspects, but police provided no additional details Saturday evening about whether anyone beyond Harris remains under investigation or at large. The Chesterfield County Police Department has continued to describe the case as an active investigation being led jointly with Virginia State University Police, with assistance from the Hanover County Sheriff's Office and the federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.
A significant law enforcement presence remained on campus through the weekend as investigators worked the scene. The university, a historically Black public institution located in Chesterfield County just south of Richmond with an enrollment of roughly 4,000 students, was not holding classes at the time of the shooting given the early morning hour, but the incident struck just two days before the start of the fall semester, with residence halls having opened only a week earlier and many incoming students having just completed the university's orientation program, known as the New Trojans Experience.
The shooting drew swift reaction from Virginia officials. Gov. Abigail Spanberger said in a statement that she and her husband were "praying for a quick recovery for those who were shot this morning at Virginia State University," adding that her thoughts were with the campus community and thanking first responders and law enforcement for their response. Virginia House of Delegates Speaker Don Scott, in a social media statement, said he was troubled by the news and was praying for those injured, particularly the person in critical condition, while U.S. Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., said he was heartbroken to learn of the shooting.
The attack is the latest in a string of firearm incidents to affect Virginia campuses and communities so far in 2026, a year that has already included a fatal shooting at Old Dominion University in Norfolk in March. It also comes amid a broader national pattern of gun violence at American colleges and universities; the Gun Violence Archive, a nonprofit that tracks shooting incidents nationwide, recorded 75 shootings at U.S. higher education institutions in 2025 alone, with a combined 100 victims.
With Harris now in custody and facing eight felony charges, attention is likely to turn toward the university's handling of the incident just before the start of the academic year and toward whatever additional details prosecutors disclose about a possible motive or the relationship, if any, between Harris and the five people shot. Classes at Virginia State University are scheduled to resume Monday as originally planned.

On Friday, more than a thousand Virginia State University freshmen gathered on campus for a ceremony celebrating the start of their college careers. They listened to life advice from former NFL quarterback Cam Newton, who told them to pursue their grandest goals. They imagined what their first college classes would be like, scheduled to start Monday. “#GreaterHappensHere,” the school posted on Facebook.
Then, shortly after midnight, gunfire erupted a quarter-mile away, just outside residence halls where students slept.
Five people were shot, leaving one critically wounded, in an incident that involved “multiple suspects,” according to the university. It noted that one of the four people with non-life-threatening injuries was a student.
Officers responded to the scene at 1:28 a.m., according to authorities, and the campus in Petersburg, Virginia, remained locked down past dawn.
On Saturday morning, the university warned that a significant law enforcement presence remained at the 3300 block of Boisseau Street. Chesterfield County Police are leading the investigation, with help from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.
On the school’s Facebook page, worried parents posted prayers and frustrations, despondent that students’ first weekend was marred by violence.
“This is sad. I was just on campus yesterday with my son,” one woman wrote.
“We just dropped our daughter off hours before this happened,” wrote another. “There needs to be heightened security for the campus. Period.”
One alumnus wrote that he and his wife had visited campus for a “stroll down ‘beautiful memories lane.’”
“When these type of events happen it’s terrifying to know that students, faculty, and visitors cannot enjoy the same level of peace that we had while we were there,” he added. “Prayers for the VSU community, immediate and extended.”
About 5,700 students attend Virginia State, a historically Black college and university a half-hour drive from Richmond.
The school has endured several incidents of gun violence on or near its campus in recent years. In 2024, it locked down at least three times because of gunfire that left five people, including a teenager, injured. In 2025, someone was shot in the leg near a campus basketball court, and a man was killed in a parking lot close to the school.
